heroStrategy.headline: Deliver Exceptional Customer Support with Zoho Desk

floatingChips: Digital License Delivered to Your Email
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected split hero with the product UI anchored on the left inside layered dashboard frames, while the copy sits on the right in a clean editorial stack. Keep the hero bright and white-first with orange as the dominant action color, but make the visual richer through a subtle orange-to-peach mesh gradient, thin grid lines, and floating support chips. The product image should show Zoho Desk’s ticket workflow, omnichannel inbox, and AI assistant at once. Follow with alternating feature sections: first light, then dark with light text, then light, then dark. Use at least two decorative treatment sections with gradient meshes and orb accents. H1 must be 60px+ for impact, with H2 at 36px+ and a crisp hierarchy. Avoid generic SaaS styling; make it feel premium, organized, and high-trust.

repetitionBreakers: Open with a dynamic split hero using orange brand energy and a product mockup.

Alternate the next product block into a split-panel layout to avoid visual repetition.
End with a high-contrast pricing-to-CTA closing sequence and a testimonial carousel.
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Desk Pricing, Features & Support Workflow Overview
blueprint.metaDescription: Discover Zoho Desk for streamlined ticket management, omnichannel customer support, AI assistance, and workflow automation. See how it works, trusted logos, features, pricing, and testimonials.

sections.backgroundTreatment: brand-gradient with subtle dashboard-panel overlays and floating support chips
sections.designNote: Content-first split hero to match the ad promise immediately. Headline should answer what it is, subheadline should clarify who it is for, and the CTA must be the single primary action: Get started. Keep a compact benefit checklist beside the copy and show the Zoho Desk UI mockup on the right. The hero should feel dynamic and trust-building, with the product visible above the fold.

sections.backgroundTreatment: light editorial band with numbered step cards
sections.designNote: Insert a 3-step process section immediately after the hero to satisfy warm traffic expectations and compress the onboarding story into under 60 seconds. Use three concise steps: capture requests, organize and automate, resolve with AI and channels. Keep it highly scannable and visually distinct from the hero with a softer grey background and a more structured card rhythm.

Use 3-6 recognisable customer logos in a clean static flex-wrap grid. Because the input only guarantees proof at a broad level and not specific logo names, keep this as a restrained logo band rather than a heavy testimonial block. Place it early to reinforce confidence before the product details deepen.

Convert the first product section into a spotlight-plus-grid block with a strong left-side feature spotlight and supporting feature cards. Focus on the click-driving ideas: omnichannel support, ticket management, workflow automation, and AI assistance. Avoid a generic SaaS grid; the section should feel like a guided product argument with one dominant feature lane and supporting proof points.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: Make Smarter Support Decisions with Zia AI

sections.designNote: Alternate the next product block into a split-panel layout to break the rhythm and give the AI story more editorial weight. Use a visual-first left panel for Zia AI and a compact feature list on the right: AI-powered responses, sentiment analysis, auto-tagging, and conversation intelligence. This section should feel more immersive and slightly more technical than the first product block.

Combine integrations and customization into a dense accordion-with-visual section because there are many features and the page is long. Use expandable groups for CRM, collaboration, telephony, e-commerce, workflows, layouts, blueprints, extensions, and help center. This keeps the section manageable without flattening it into a static card grid.

Present pricing as a focused center card with the included capabilities clearly listed. Keep the CTA family consistent and conversion-led with Get started only. This should feel clean and trustworthy, not aggressive, with the plan contents acting as the final decision support before testimonials.

Use a testimonial carousel because there are 4+ testimonials. Keep the cards quote-led with compact role labels and company names where available. This section should restore credibility after pricing and introduce a human voice without repeating the earlier logo proof pattern.

End with a centered conversion card or compact lead capture block that reiterates the product value and gives the final Get started CTA. Keep it visually cleaner than the hero and slightly more grounded, so the page closes with confidence rather than noise.
